title: A protocol for full-rotation soft X-ray tomography of single cells
protocol: Spin polystyrene microbeads at 10000×g for 2 min using a centrifuge.
Remove supernatant and resuspend beads in PBS 1×.
Repeat washing in PBS 1× twice.
Load 1.1–3.0 μL of bead mixture into a glass capillary using a micro-loading tip.
Proceed with cryofixation.
Prepare trimmed capillaries with a tip size suiting the cell diameter as described in Glass capillary preparation.
Count cell density using hemocytometer or an automated cell counter.
Choose beads of the same size as capillary tip and calculate volume to ensure 1:1 ratio of cells and beads.
Spin microbeads at 10000×g for 2 min using a centrifuge.
Remove supernatant and resuspend beads in PBS 1×.
Repeat washing in PBS 1× twice.
Spin cells in a 15-mL tube at 300×g for 10 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 1.5 ml tube together with microbeads.
Spin mix of microbeads and cells at 300×g for 10 minutes.
Remove supernatant from the mixture.
Resuspend beads/cells mixture in 20–30 μL PBS 1×.
Mix resuspended beads/cells by tapping with your index finger.
Load 1.1–3.0 μL of beads/cells mixture into a glass capillary using a micro-loading tip.
Wait a few seconds before removing the micro-loading tip from the glass tube.
Check the quality of prepared capillaries under a light microscope.
Discard capillaries with low numbers of cells or lower ratios of cells and beads.
Repeat steps until the desired number of capillaries containing specimens is prepared.
Document approximate number of cells and beads in each capillary visible under a light microscope (optional).
Cryo-fix specimens within 1 to 2 hours prior to X-ray imaging to prevent radiation damage.
Put a puck and storage box in the freezing apparatus.
Cool down the freezing machine with liquid nitrogen.
Home the robot.
Fill the propane well and put it in position for plunging.
Attach tubes for dry nitrogen.
Purge with dry nitrogen to cleanse the system from contaminants.
Set up the plunger according to the type of samples to freeze down.
Ensure the height of the propane well is set correctly.
Set up the heater for dry nitrogen at 30°C.
Set up the heater for the viewing glass window at 30°C.
Mount the capillary on the grabber.
Plunge the capillary in the propane well.
Automatically transfer the capillary from the propane well to an empty position in the storage puck.
Take beamline safety and operation course.
Use appropriate personal protective equipment.
Check the beam status of the ALS.
Open the Branchline Equipment Protective System (EPS) if the beam is available for user operation.
Reset the pressure on the system.
Ensure that the status of all beamline components is correct.
Adjust the pressure gauge IG207 to around 10−5 Torr.
Adjust the pressure gauge IG206 to around 10−7 Torr.
Adjust the pressure gauge IG205 to around 10−8 Torr.
Adjust the pressure gauges IG204 and IG203 to around 10−10 Torr.
Open the vacuum valves from right to left: first VVR204, followed by VVR203 and VVR202 to let the X-ray beam come through into the microscope.
Turn on the GUI and activate the microscope.
Home the sample stage, filters, and camera of the microscope.
Move the X-ray camera towards the sample stage to get a big field-of-view and check the intactness of the silicon nitrate window.
Fill the liquid nitrogen cold traps of the KZP and MZP box.
Align the microscope at ambient temperature by translating the MZP and the KZP to the center of the FOV.
Initialize the nitrogen and helium flow.
Fill the zeolite tank with liquid nitrogen to cool down helium.
Start cooling down the cryobox with liquid nitrogen.
Turn on the heaters on top of the cryobox to avoid ice accumulation in the sample chamber.
Re-align the microscope after cooling down as described.
Drive the camera back to its initial position after re-alignment.
Make a snapshot with the scanning mode to check the homogeneity of the illumination.
Re-adjust the MZP and, if necessary, the KZP for proper alignment.
Maximize the cold helium flow of the cryo-transfer device to keep the sample vitrified.
Transfer the capillary to the sample chamber using clamps to suspend the specimen.
Grab the capillary by translating the sample stage in Y and Z axes.
Attach the capillary to a goniometer using a pin.
Press "sample transfer complete" to automatically release the clamps and send the sample into the chamber for alignment with a Borescope.
Align the capillary tip in the center of the X-ray beam under low magnification Borescope view.
Select "alignment done" to finalize the position.
If ice buildup on the capillary surface is observed under the microscope, increase the cryobox temperature to -90°C for 60 seconds and then cool down the microscope to −150°C.
Find the tip of the capillary under the X-rays and align the capillary with higher resolution until the capillary is in the center of the FOV.
Translate the capillary vertically to find the cell within the FOV.
Check rotation center again.
If not centered, repeat step 37.
Perform fine alignment of the capillary rotation below the cell of interest to avoid multiple exposure and high X-ray dose.
Set data acquisition parameters to 2 × 2 binning.
Set step size to 2° per step and acquire 92 projections for 180° data acquisition.
For sensitive cells, set step size to 4° to distribute X-ray radiation dose evenly over 360°.
Set the exposure time between 200 ms and 500 ms based on sample thickness and beam flux.
Move the sample out of the X-ray beam.
Select an X-ray absorption filter for reference images.
Move the sample back to the center of the FOV.
Switch on auto-correction procedure to keep the capillary centered in the FOV during data acquisition.
Start the data acquisition.
Collect two sets of 10 flat-field images before and after the acquisition of projection images.
Shift X-ray camera closer to capillary if cell is larger than field of view horizontally.
Shift specimen vertically by 80% of the field of view for stitching of 3D datasets when necessary.
Repeat tomographic data acquisition for each subsequent cell in the capillary.
Select MZP in use on microscope, pixel size and step size will be recalculated automatically.
Dispose used capillary immediately after imaging is complete.
Transfer next specimen into microscope once previous one has been removed.
Repeat alignment and tomography acquisition steps for new specimens.
Collect approximately 40 samples during an 8-hour working period.
Shut down the microscope when all specimens are imaged.
Slowly bring the microscope to ambient (20°C–24°C) temperature.
Reduce the flow of dry nitrogen.
Set de-ice of the microscope to 40°C for 360 s.
Repeat the de-ice procedure until liquid nitrogen in the sample chamber has evaporated.
Close the nitrogen and helium flow.
Set the heaters on the sample box to continue heating to 24°C for 6 hours after shutting down.
Open SXT dataset with Fiji software containing polystyrene beads of known size.
Take measurements of bead size in pixels.
Calculate the effective pixel size.
Repeat step for different X-ray camera positions along the beam if necessary.
Segment 80–100 polystyrene beads with a diameter of 6 μm using thresholding.
Multiply X-ray absorption intensity by the pixel area, i.e., 1/(2·pixel size) in μm.
Compare the X-ray LAC of the beads with expected 0.81 ± 0.03 μm−1.

Estimate the X-ray energy window used for SXT imaging by comparing experimental LAC with expected absorption for polystyrene (C8H8) from atomic scattering database maintained by CXRO at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
Segment individual components of reconstructed data to analyze and quantify volume and mutual distances of cellular organelles.
Perform segmentation manually on soft x-ray tomography datasets, particularly for samples of unknown variability like virally infected cells.
Save reconstructed tomograms in .mrc format.
Analyze segmented data using commercial software Amira-Avizo (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Normalize the LAC value of each pixel in tomographic data (.mrc file) as described in step 56.
Perform edge-preserving smoothing to simplify outlining of organelles and smooth visualization of SXT data.
Define a set of materials (nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum, cytosol, lipid droplets) in the segmentation editor for infected cells.
Add unknown materials for virus-associated organelles like double membrane vesicles.
Adjust the contrast to enhance the edge of the structure of interest.
Segment cytosol using the magic wand tool.
Select "same material only" and "all slices".
Adjust the range of LAC values until all parts of the cells are selected.
Add the selected area to the material (cytosol).
Use the brush tool to outline the edge of the nucleus.
Fill the outlined region by pressing F.
Add the filled region to the nucleus material.
Repeat outlining and filling for every tenth orthoslice.
Select all slices and interpolate the labels.
If desired, segment heterochromatin and euchromatin semi-automatically based on their bimodal distribution within the nucleus volume.
Segment mitochondria, ER, lipid droplets, and intracellular vesicles semi-automatically.
Select Magic Wand tool
Define threshold for X-ray absorption for lipid droplets at 0.75 ± 0.09 μm−1
Define threshold for X-ray absorption for mitochondria at 0.45 ± 0.03 μm−1
Define threshold for X-ray absorption for ER at 0.24 ± 0.04 μm−1
Select voxel corresponding to the organelle
Add selected voxel to material
Repeat until all organelles are segmented
Optional: Remove thin-walled glass capillary by extracting its internal content if necessary
Retrieve physical features and values of each set of organelles using Material Statistics in Amira
Export individual label fields for use in custom-made analysis pipelines
